title: Contractible homotopy fibers detect equivalences of spaces
statement: Use spaces, weak equivalences, contractibility and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $f:P\to Q$ be a map of small Kan complexes. Then $f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if, for every vertex $q\in Q$, the homotopy fiber $P\times_{Q,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Q)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Q}\{q\}$ is contractible. In particular, every homotopy fiber of an equivalence of spaces is contractible; this assertion concerns homotopy fibers and not ordinary set-theoretic fibers.

source.place: Kerodon, Remark 3.4.0.6, tag 0328 (Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag); uses Proposition 3.3.7.6 and the path-space fibration replacement Read online; not archived in literature/. No matching Stacks tag for this assertion.

proof.text: Apply the path-space replacement to f. The resulting projection p:E_f→Q is a Kan fibration, its constant-path inclusion i:P→E_f is a weak homotopy equivalence over Q, and the strict fiber of p at each q is exactly the homotopy fiber appearing in the statement.

source.place: Remark 3.4.0.6 (tag 0328), factorization of f through the path fibration of Example 3.1.8.10 (tag 0101)

proof.text: Assume f is a weak homotopy equivalence. Since f=p∘i and i is a weak homotopy equivalence, cancellation for the bijection on components and the isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups gives that p is a weak homotopy equivalence. The Kan-fibration fiber criterion then says every strict fiber of p is weakly contractible, and the path-space identification in Step 1 transfers this to every homotopy fiber of f.

Conversely, assume every homotopy fiber of f is contractible. By Step 1 the strict fibers of p are weakly contractible, so the Kan-fibration fiber criterion makes p a weak homotopy equivalence. Together with the weak equivalence i and f=p∘i, cancellation for the same component bijection and homotopy-group isomorphisms gives that f is a weak homotopy equivalence.
